commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. # Planning: Tokenizer Fertility and Cross-Lingual Transfer Degradation

Written before any model was trained or evaluated. Deviations are logged at the bottom.

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Multilingual encoders are fine-tuned on English and deployed on other languages. If the
transfer loss is driven by how finely the shared subword vocabulary fragments a language,
that is something an engineer can fix (vocabulary allocation, tokenizer choice), whereas
typological distance is not. Knowing which of the two predicts the loss tells practitioners
where to spend effort and which languages are at risk before any labelled data exists.

### Gap in Existing Work
(The pre-gathered literature review was missing from the workspace; this is from my own
knowledge of the literature.) Rust et al. 2021 ("How Good is Your Tokenizer?") show that
mBERT over-segments some languages relative to monolingual tokenizers and that this hurts
monolingual downstream quality. Ács 2019 introduced fertility for mBERT. Lauscher et al.
2020 and Pires et al. 2019 predict zero-shot transfer from typological (URIEL) distance and
pretraining corpus size; Wu & Dredze 2020 show low-resource languages are poorly served.
What is missing is a head-to-head comparison in which fertility, typological distance and
pretraining size are competing predictors of the *same* transfer drops, across several
tasks and two different tokenizers, with a check of whether fertility is anything more than
a proxy for the other two.

### Our Novel Contribution
1. A direct variance-explained comparison (fertility vs. URIEL distances vs. pretraining
   size) over 71 target languages x 3 tasks x 2 models, with bootstrap CIs.
2. A test of the specific numerical claims: R^2 in 40-60%, a 2.5x threshold with >30% drop.
3. Two designs that separate fertility from language identity: a within-language contrast
   (same language, two tokenizers) and a causal intervention (same language, same model,
   artificially finer segmentation of English at test time).

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (zero-shot transfer, 3 tasks x 2 models x multiple seeds): produces the dependent
  variable. Three tasks so the result is not a property of one benchmark; two models so it
  is not a property of one tokenizer.
- Exp 2 (language features): fertility, URIEL distances, pretraining size - the predictors.
- Exp 3 (regression analysis): answers the hypothesis' four sub-claims.
- Exp 4 (within-language tokenizer contrast): language, typology and test data are held
  fixed; only the tokenizer/model differs. Tests whether fertility differences track drop
  differences once typology cannot vary.
- Exp 5 (over-segmentation intervention on English): the only experiment here that
  manipulates fertility. Tells us how much damage fragmentation alone can do.

## Research Question
Does the tokenizer fertility ratio of a target language (relative to English) explain
40-60% of the between-language variance in zero-shot transfer degradation, more than
typological distance does, with a catastrophic regime above 2.5x, and independently of
pretraining data size?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: R^2 of `drop ~ fertility_ratio` lies in [0.40, 0.60].
- H2: R^2(fertility) > R^2(typological distance).
- H3: languages with fertility ratio > 2.5 have drop > 30; languages below mostly do not.
- H4: the fertility effect survives controlling for pretraining data size (partial
  correlation stays clearly non-zero; no fertility x size interaction needed to explain it).

Variables. DV: `drop = score_en - score_target` in points (accuracy for XNLI/SIB-200, span
F1 for NER), mean over seeds. Also relative drop `100*drop/score_en`. IVs defined below.

## Proposed Methodology

### Models
`bert-base-multilingual-cased` (WordPiece, 119k) and `xlm-roberta-base` (SentencePiece
unigram, 250k). Both are the standard zero-shot transfer baselines; they need fine-tuning
and per-language tokenization, so local models are required. No LLM API is used: no
OpenRouter key is present in the environment, and API LLMs do not give a clean
"train on English only" transfer setting.

### Tasks and data (all English-train, zero-shot test)
| Task | HF dataset | Train | Target languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| NLI | `facebook/xnli` | en MNLI 393k | 14 |
| NER | `unimelb-nlp/wikiann` | en 20k | 71 |
| Topic classification | `Davlan/sib200` (Flores-200 sentences) | en 701 | 71 |

Language set (fixed in advance): every language that is (a) in mBERT's pretraining list,
(b) in XLM-R's pretraining list, (c) in Flores-200/SIB-200, (d) in WikiANN. 72 languages
including English. Restricting to languages seen by both models removes the "unseen
language" confound.

### Predictors
- Fertility (primary): mean subword tokens per whitespace word on the language's 1,004
  Flores-200 sentences (SIB-200 train+dev+test text), divided by the same quantity for
  English. Chinese, Japanese, Thai and Burmese are not whitespace-segmented, so they are
  excluded from the primary analysis (67 targets; 12 for XNLI).
- Fertility (secondary, all 71): parallel token ratio = total tokens on the Flores
  sentences / total tokens on the English translations of the same sentences.
- Robustness: fertility on WikiANN's own pre-tokenized test words.
- Typological distance from English: cosine distance between URIEL (lang2vec) kNN-imputed
  feature vectors: syntactic (primary baseline, the one used most in prior work),
  phonological, inventory, genetic (family vectors), geographic. Also all five jointly.
- Pretraining size: mBERT - log10 Wikipedia article count (Wikimedia API, today's count as
  a proxy for the 2018 dump); XLM-R - log10 CC-100 size from data.statmt.org/cc-100.
- Covariates reported, not in primary tests: non-Latin script, UNK rate, share of words
  split into 2+ pieces.

### Training
Standard recipes, no per-language tuning, model selection on English dev only.
- XNLI: 2 epochs, bs 32, lr 2e-5, max len 128, 3 seeds.
- NER: 5 epochs, bs 32, lr 3e-5, first-subword labelling, seqeval span F1, 3 seeds.
- SIB-200: 20 epochs, bs 16, lr 2e-5, best English-dev epoch, 5 seeds (small train set).

### Baselines
Predictor baselines for fertility: syntactic distance, each other URIEL distance, all URIEL
distances jointly, log pretraining size, non-Latin script indicator. Performance
baselines: majority class / chance for each task, to put drops in context.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
Unit of analysis: language, within each of the 6 model x task cells.
- H1: OLS R^2 and Spearman rho, 95% percentile bootstrap CI over languages (10,000
  resamples). Supported in a cell if the R^2 point estimate is in [0.40, 0.60].
- H2: bootstrap CI of R^2(fertility) - R^2(syntactic). Also against the joint URIEL model
  using adjusted R^2. Supported if the difference CI excludes 0 in most cells.
- H3: among languages with ratio > 2.5, share with absolute drop > 30 points and share
  with relative drop > 30%; same shares below 2.5; Fisher exact test. Report how many
  languages exceed 2.5 at all. Linear vs. hinge-at-2.5 fit as a nonlinearity check.
- H4: partial correlation of fertility with drop given log size; then given log size +
  syntactic distance; OLS with fertility x size interaction. Unique R^2 of fertility in
  the full model (fertility + size + syntactic).
- Pooled: all cells stacked, drop z-scored within cell, bootstrap clustered by language.
- Holm correction across the 6 cells for each family of tests. alpha = 0.05.
- Seed variability: SD across seeds of each language's score.

## Expected Outcomes
Support: fertility R^2 0.4-0.6 in most cells, beating syntactic distance, partial
correlation given size still large, a visible break near 2.5x, and a dose-response in the
intervention. Refutation: fertility R^2 well below 0.4 or not above the baselines; the
effect vanishing once size is controlled; few or no languages beyond 2.5x, or those
languages not failing; the within-language contrast showing no relationship.
My prior: fertility correlates with drop but is heavily entangled with pretraining size
(the vocabulary is learned from the same corpus) and with script.

## Timeline
Setup and metadata 30 min; training code 45 min; training runs ~60 min wall on 4 GPUs;
intervention 20 min; analysis 45 min; report 30 min.

## Potential Challenges
- /data is full (6 GB): venv under ~/.cache (symlinked), HF cache and checkpoints in
  /dev/shm, checkpoints deleted at the end.
- SIB-200 test sets are 204 sentences: per-language accuracy has SE ~3 points. Mitigated
  with 5 seeds; noise ceiling estimated.
- XNLI has only 14 targets: wide CIs, reported as such.
- Few languages may exceed 2.5x: if so H3 is reported as untestable/unsupported at that
  threshold rather than moving the threshold.

## Success Criteria
All six cells trained with sane English scores (XNLI ~81/84, NER ~83, SIB ~85+), every
pre-specified test reported with CIs whichever way it comes out.

## Deviations from plan
(filled in during execution)

  a proxy for the 2018 dump); XLM-R - log10 CC-100 size from data.statmt.org/cc-100.
- Covariates reported, not in primary tests: non-Latin script, UNK rate, share of words
  split into 2+ pieces.

### Training
Standard recipes, no per-language tuning, model selection on English dev only.
- XNLI: 2 epochs, bs 32, lr 2e-5, max len 128, 3 seeds.
- NER: 5 epochs, bs 32, lr 3e-5, first-subword labelling, seqeval span F1, 3 seeds.
- SIB-200: 20 epochs, bs 16, lr 2e-5, best English-dev epoch, 5 seeds (small train set).

### Baselines
Predictor baselines for fertility: syntactic distance, each other URIEL distance, all URIEL
distances jointly, log pretraining size, non-Latin script indicator. Performance
baselines: majority class / chance for each task, to put drops in context.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
Unit of analysis: language, within each of the 6 model x task cells.
- H1: OLS R^2 and Spearman rho, 95% percentile bootstrap CI over languages (10,000
  resamples). Supported in a cell if the R^2 point estimate is in [0.40, 0.60].
- H2: bootstrap CI of R^2(fertility) - R^2(syntactic). Also against the joint URIEL model
  using adjusted R^2. Supported if the difference CI excludes 0 in most cells.
- H3: among languages with ratio > 2.5, share with absolute drop > 30 points and share
  with relative drop > 30%; same shares below 2.5; Fisher exact test. Report how many
  languages exceed 2.5 at all. Linear vs. hinge-at-2.5 fit as a nonlinearity check.
- H4: partial correlation of fertility with drop given log size; then given log size +
  syntactic distance; OLS with fertility x size interaction. Unique R^2 of fertility in
  the full model (fertility + size + syntactic).
- Pooled: all cells stacked, drop z-scored within cell, bootstrap clustered by language.
- Holm correction across the 6 cells for each family of tests. alpha = 0.05.
- Seed variability: SD across seeds of each language's score.

## Expected Outcomes
Support: fertility R^2 0.4-0.6 in most cells, beating syntactic distance, partial
correlation given size still large, a visible break near 2.5x, and a dose-response in the
intervention. Refutation: fertility R^2 well below 0.4 or not above the baselines; the
effect vanishing once size is controlled; few or no languages beyond 2.5x, or those
languages not failing; the within-language contrast showing no relationship.
My prior: fertility correlates with drop but is heavily entangled with pretraining size
(the vocabulary is learned from the same corpus) and with script.

## Timeline
Setup and metadata 30 min; training code 45 min; training runs ~60 min wall on 4 GPUs;
intervention 20 min; analysis 45 min; report 30 min.

## Potential Challenges
- /data is full (6 GB): venv under ~/.cache (symlinked), HF cache and checkpoints in
  /dev/shm, checkpoints deleted at the end.
- SIB-200 test sets are 204 sentences: per-language accuracy has SE ~3 points. Mitigated
  with 5 seeds; noise ceiling estimated.
- XNLI has only 14 targets: wide CIs, reported as such.
- Few languages may exceed 2.5x: if so H3 is reported as untestable/unsupported at that
  threshold rather than moving the threshold.

## Success Criteria
All six cells trained with sane English scores (XNLI ~81/84, NER ~83, SIB ~85+), every
pre-specified test reported with CIs whichever way it comes out.

"""Fine-tune a multilingual encoder on English and evaluate zero-shot on every target language.

Usage: python src/train.py --task {xnli,ner,sib} --model {mbert,xlmr} --seed N [--smoke]
Writes results/model_outputs/{task}_{model}_s{seed}.json (+ .npz predictions) and a
checkpoint under CKPT_DIR for the intervention experiment.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
from seqeval.metrics import f1_score
from transformers import (AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoModelForTokenClassification,
                          AutoTokenizer, get_linear_schedule_with_warmup)

from data import DEV_SPLIT, LOADERS, NER_LABELS, NUM_LABELS
from langs import CKPT_DIR, MODELS, RESULTS, WIKI, XNLI_LANGS

HP = {  # standard recipes; nothing is tuned on target languages
    "xnli": dict(epochs=2, bs=32, lr=2e-5, max_len=128),
    "ner": dict(epochs=5, bs=32, lr=3e-5, max_len=256),
    "sib": dict(epochs=20, bs=16, lr=2e-5, max_len=128),
}
TASK_LANGS = {"xnli": XNLI_LANGS, "ner": WIKI, "sib": WIKI}


def set_seed(seed):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def encode(tok, task, df, max_len):
    """Standard tokenization. Returns a list of feature dicts (python lists, unpadded)."""
    if task == "xnli":
        enc = tok(list(df.premise), list(df.hypothesis), truncation=True, max_length=max_len)
    elif task == "sib":
        enc = tok(list(df.text), truncation=True, max_length=max_len)
    else:
        enc = tok([list(t) for t in df.tokens], is_split_into_words=True, truncation=True, max_length=max_len)
    feats = []
    for i in range(len(df)):
        f = {"input_ids": enc["input_ids"][i]}
        if "token_type_ids" in enc:
            f["token_type_ids"] = enc["token_type_ids"][i]
        if task == "ner":
            # label only the first subword of each word; -100 elsewhere
            tags, lab, prev = df.ner_tags.iloc[i], [], None
            for w in enc.word_ids(i):
                lab.append(-100 if w is None or w == prev else int(tags[w]))
                prev = w
            f["labels"] = lab
        else:
            f["labels"] = int(df.label.iloc[i])
        feats.append(f)
    return feats


def collate(feats, pad_id, device):
    n = max(len(f["input_ids"]) for f in feats)
    ids = torch.full((len(feats), n), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    mask = torch.zeros((len(feats), n), dtype=torch.long)
    batch = {}
    if "token_type_ids" in feats[0]:
        tt = torch.zeros((len(feats), n), dtype=torch.long)
    seq_labels = isinstance(feats[0]["labels"], list)
    lab = torch.full((len(feats), n), -100, dtype=torch.long) if seq_labels else torch.tensor([f["labels"] for f in feats])
    for i, f in enumerate(feats):
        k = len(f["input_ids"])
        ids[i, :k] = torch.tensor(f["input_ids"])
        mask[i, :k] = 1
        if "token_type_ids" in f:
            tt[i, :k] = torch.tensor(f["token_type_ids"])
        if seq_labels:
            lab[i, :k] = torch.tensor(f["labels"])
    batch.update(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=mask, labels=lab)
    if "token_type_ids" in feats[0]:
        batch["token_type_ids"] = tt
    return {k: v.to(device) for k, v in batch.items()}


@torch.no_grad()
def predict(model, feats, pad_id, device, bs=256):
    """Returns per-example predictions in the original order (list of ints / list of int lists)."""
    model.eval()
    order = np.argsort([len(f["input_ids"]) for f in feats])
    out = [None] * len(feats)
    for s in range(0, len(order), bs):
        idx = order[s:s + bs]
        b = collate([feats[i] for i in idx], pad_id, device)
        labels = b.pop("labels")
        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
            pred = model(**b).logits.argmax(-1)
        if labels.dim() == 2:
            for j, i in enumerate(idx):
                out[i] = pred[j][labels[j] != -100].tolist()
        else:
            for j, i in enumerate(idx):
                out[i] = int(pred[j])
    return out


def score(task, feats, preds, df):
    """Accuracy (xnli, sib) or seqeval span F1 (ner), in percent."""
    if task != "ner":
        return 100 * float(np.mean(np.array(preds) == df.label.values))
    gold, hyp = [], []
    for p, tags in zip(preds, df.ner_tags):
        # words lost to truncation are predicted as O
        p = list(p) + [0] * (len(tags) - len(p))
        gold.append([NER_LABELS[t] for t in tags])
        hyp.append([NER_LABELS[t] for t in p])
    return 100 * f1_score(gold, hyp)


def load_model(task, name_or_path):
    cls = AutoModelForTokenClassification if task == "ner" else AutoModelForSequenceClassification
    return cls.from_pretrained(name_or_path, num_labels=NUM_LABELS[task])


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--task", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="tiny run to validate the pipeline")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    hp, device = HP[a.task], "cuda"
    tag = f"{a.task}_{a.model}_s{a.seed}" + ("_smoke" if a.smoke else "")
    out_dir = os.path.join(RESULTS, "model_outputs")
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    set_seed(a.seed)
    t0 = time.time()

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODELS[a.model])
    load = LOADERS[a.task]
    train_df, dev_df = load("en", "train"), load("en", DEV_SPLIT[a.task])
    langs = TASK_LANGS[a.task]
    if a.smoke:
        train_df, langs = train_df.iloc[:2000], langs[:3]
    train, dev = encode(tok, a.task, train_df, hp["max_len"]), encode(tok, a.task, dev_df, hp["max_len"])
    print(f"[{tag}] train={len(train)} dev={len(dev)} tokenized in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)

    model = load_model(a.task, MODELS[a.model]).to(device)
    no_decay = ["bias", "LayerNorm.weight"]
    params = [
        {"params": [p for n, p in model.named_parameters() if not any(x in n for x in no_decay)], "weight_decay": 0.01},
        {"params": [p for n, p in model.named_parameters() if any(x in n for x in no_decay)], "weight_decay": 0.0},
    ]
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=hp["lr"])
    epochs = 1 if a.smoke else hp["epochs"]
    steps = epochs * ((len(train) + hp["bs"] - 1) // hp["bs"])
    sched = get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(opt, int(0.1 * steps), steps)
    scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler("cuda")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(a.seed)

    best_dev, best_state, dev_hist, step = -1, None, [], 0
    for ep in range(epochs):
        model.train()
        perm = rng.permutation(len(train))
        for s in range(0, len(perm), hp["bs"]):
            b = collate([train[i] for i in perm[s:s + hp["bs"]]], tok.pad_token_id, device)
            with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
                loss = model(**b).loss
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            scaler.scale(loss).backward()
            scaler.unscale_(opt)
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
            scaler.step(opt)
            scaler.update()
            sched.step()
            step += 1
            if step % 1000 == 0:
                print(f"[{tag}] step {step}/{steps} loss {loss.item():.3f} {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
        d = score(a.task, dev, predict(model, dev, tok.pad_token_id, device), dev_df)
        dev_hist.append(d)
        print(f"[{tag}] epoch {ep+1} en-dev {d:.2f}", flush=True)
        # SIB's train set is tiny, so keep the best English-dev epoch; other tasks use the last epoch
        if a.task == "sib" and d > best_dev:
            best_dev, best_state = d, {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
    if best_state is not None:
        model.load_state_dict(best_state)
    assert np.isfinite(loss.item())

    scores, preds_out = {}, {}
    for lang in langs:
        df = load(lang, "test")
        feats = encode(tok, a.task, df, hp["max_len"])
        preds = predict(model, feats, tok.pad_token_id, device)
        scores[lang] = score(a.task, feats, preds, df)
        if a.task != "ner":

from langs import MODELS, WIKI, XNLI_LANGS

jobs = [(load_xnli, "en", "train"), (load_xnli, "en", "validation"), (load_ner, "en", "train"),
        (load_ner, "en", "validation")]
jobs += [(load_xnli, l, "test") for l in XNLI_LANGS]
jobs += [(load_ner, l, "test") for l in WIKI]
jobs += [(load_sib, l, s) for l in WIKI for s in ("train", "dev", "test")]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    sizes = list(ex.map(lambda j: len(j[0](j[1], j[2])), jobs))
for (fn, l, s), n in zip(jobs, sizes):
    print(fn.__name__, l, s, n)
for m in MODELS.values():
    AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(m)
    AutoModel.from_pretrained(m)
    print("cached", m)

"""Run every fine-tuning job on shared GPUs.

The GPUs are shared with other users' jobs, so each job is placed on the GPU with the most
free memory, jobs that die (e.g. OOM when a neighbour grows) are retried, and finished jobs
(result json present) are skipped, which makes the script resumable.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from langs import RESULTS, ROOT

SEEDS = {"ner": [1, 2, 3], "sib": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "xnli": [1, 2, 3]}
NEED_MB, PER_GPU, RESERVE_S, MAX_TRIES = 7000, 3, 120, 4

# cheap, many-language tasks first; XNLI (longest) last
jobs = [(t, m, s) for t in ("ner", "sib", "xnli") for s in SEEDS[t] for m in ("mbert", "xlmr")]
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    jobs = [j for j in jobs if j[0] in sys.argv[1:]]
tag = lambda j: f"{j[0]}_{j[1]}_s{j[2]}"
done = lambda j: os.path.exists(os.path.join(RESULTS, "model_outputs", tag(j) + ".json"))


def free_mb():
    out = subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"])
    return [int(x) for x in out.decode().split()]


queue = [j for j in jobs if not done(j)]
tries, running = {}, []  # running: (job, gpu, popen, start_time)
env = dict(os.environ, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True", TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false")
while queue or running:
    for r in list(running):
        job, gpu, p, t0 = r
        if p.poll() is None:
            continue
        running.remove(r)
        if done(job):
            print(f"OK   {tag(job)} gpu{gpu} {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
        else:
            tries[job] = tries.get(job, 0) + 1
            print(f"FAIL {tag(job)} gpu{gpu} try {tries[job]}", flush=True)
            if tries[job] < MAX_TRIES:
                queue.append(job)
    if queue:
        free = free_mb()
        for g in range(len(free)):
            mine = [r for r in running if r[1] == g]
            # jobs started recently have not allocated their memory yet
            free[g] -= NEED_MB * sum(time.time() - r[3] < RESERVE_S for r in mine)
            if len(mine) >= PER_GPU:
                free[g] = 0
        g = max(range(len(free)), key=lambda i: free[i])
        if free[g] >= NEED_MB:
            job = queue.pop(0)
            log = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "logs", f"train_{tag(job)}.log"), "a")
            p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "train.py"), "--task", job[0],
                                  "--model", job[1], "--seed", str(job[2])],
                                 env=dict(env, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(g)), stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            running.append((job, g, p, time.time()))
            print(f"RUN  {tag(job)} gpu{g}", flush=True)
            continue
    time.sleep(10)
missing = [tag(j) for j in jobs if not done(j)]
print("ALL DONE" if not missing else f"MISSING {missing}", flush=True)

"""Causal check: over-segment *English* test inputs and measure the score loss.

Language, model and test items are fixed; only segmentation granularity changes. Every
subword longer than `cap` characters is re-split greedily (longest match in the vocabulary,
at most `cap` characters per piece), which raises fertility without changing the text.
cap=None is the standard tokenization and must reproduce the standard English score.

Output: results/intervention.csv
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from data import LOADERS
from langs import CKPT_DIR, MODELS, RESULTS
from train import HP, load_model, predict, score

CAPS = [None, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1]


class Segmenter:
    def __init__(self, mkey):
        self.tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODELS[mkey])
        self.vocab = self.tok.get_vocab()
        self.bert = mkey == "mbert"
        self.cache = {}

    def _mark(self, body, word_initial_piece, first_chunk):
        """Vocabulary form of a chunk: mBERT marks continuations (##x), XLM-R marks word starts (▁x)."""
        if self.bert:
            return body if (word_initial_piece and first_chunk) else "##" + body
        return "▁" + body if (word_initial_piece and first_chunk) else body

    def pieces(self, word, cap):
        key = (word, cap)
        if key in self.cache:
            return self.cache[key]
        out = []
        for p in self.tok.tokenize(word):
            if self.bert:
                initial, body = not p.startswith("##"), p[2:] if p.startswith("##") else p
            else:
                initial, body = p.startswith("▁"), p.lstrip("▁")
            if cap is None or len(body) <= cap:
                out.append(p)
                continue
            i = 0
            while i < len(body):
                for n in range(min(cap, len(body) - i), 0, -1):
                    cand = self._mark(body[i:i + n], initial, i == 0)
                    if cand in self.vocab:
                        out.append(cand)
                        i += n
                        break
                else:
                    if not self.bert and initial and i == 0 and "▁" in self.vocab:
                        out.append("▁")  # emit the bare word-start marker, retry the chunk unmarked
                        initial = False
                        continue
                    out.append(self.tok.unk_token)
                    i += 1
        self.cache[key] = out
        return out

    def words_to_ids(self, words, cap):
        """Returns (ids, index of the first piece of each word)."""
        ids, starts = [], []
        for w in words:
            p = self.pieces(w, cap)
            if not p:
                continue
            starts.append(len(ids))
            ids.extend(self.tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(p))
        return ids, starts


def build(seg, task, df, cap, max_len):
    """Manual equivalent of train.encode() with a segmentation cap. Also returns token/word counts."""
    tok, feats, n_tok, n_word, n_unk = seg.tok, [], 0, 0, 0
    cls, sep = tok.cls_token_id, tok.sep_token_id
    for i in range(len(df)):
        if task == "xnli":
            (a, _), (b, _) = seg.words_to_ids(df.premise.iloc[i].split(), cap), seg.words_to_ids(df.hypothesis.iloc[i].split(), cap)
            n_tok += len(a) + len(b)
            n_word += len(df.premise.iloc[i].split()) + len(df.hypothesis.iloc[i].split())
            n_unk += sum(t == tok.unk_token_id for t in a + b)
            n_special = 3 if seg.bert else 4
            while len(a) + len(b) > max_len - n_special:  # longest-first truncation
                (a if len(a) > len(b) else b).pop()
            if seg.bert:
                f = {"input_ids": [cls] + a + [sep] + b + [sep], "token_type_ids": [0] * (len(a) + 2) + [1] * (len(b) + 1)}
            else:
                f = {"input_ids": [cls] + a + [sep, sep] + b + [sep]}
            f["labels"] = int(df.label.iloc[i])
        else:
            words = df.text.iloc[i].split() if task == "sib" else list(df.tokens.iloc[i])
            ids, starts = seg.words_to_ids(words, cap)
            n_tok += len(ids)
            n_word += len(words)
            n_unk += sum(t == tok.unk_token_id for t in ids)
            ids = ids[:max_len - 2]
            f = {"input_ids": [cls] + ids + [sep]}
            if seg.bert:
                f["token_type_ids"] = [0] * len(f["input_ids"])
            if task == "sib":
                f["labels"] = int(df.label.iloc[i])
            else:
                lab = [-100] * len(f["input_ids"])
                for s, t in zip(starts, df.ner_tags.iloc[i]):
                    if s < len(ids):
                        lab[s + 1] = int(t)
                f["labels"] = lab
        feats.append(f)
    return feats, n_tok / n_word, n_unk / n_tok


def main():
    rows = []
    for ck in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CKPT_DIR, "*_s*"))):
        tag = os.path.basename(ck)
        task, mkey, seed = tag.split("_")
        std = json.load(open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "model_outputs", tag + ".json")))["scores"]["en"]
        seg, df = Segmenter(mkey), LOADERS[task]("en", "test")
        model = load_model(task, ck).cuda()
        base_tpw = None
        for cap in CAPS:
            feats, tpw, unk = build(seg, task, df, cap, HP[task]["max_len"])
            s = score(task, feats, predict(model, feats, seg.tok.pad_token_id, "cuda"), df)
            if cap is None:
                base_tpw, base = tpw, s
                # manual pipeline must match the standard tokenizer pipeline
                assert abs(s - std) < 0.5, (tag, s, std)
            rows.append(dict(task=task, model=mkey, seed=int(seed[1:]), cap=cap or 0, tok_per_word=tpw,
                             fert_ratio=tpw / base_tpw, unk_rate=unk, score=s, drop=base - s, std_score=std))
            print(rows[-1], flush=True)
        del model
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(os.path.join(RESULTS, "intervention.csv"), index=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        self.bert = mkey == "mbert"
        self.cache = {}

        if self.bert:
            return body if (word_initial_piece and first_chunk) else "##" + body
        return "▁" + body if (word_initial_piece and first_chunk) else body

    def pieces(self, word, cap):
        key = (word, cap)
        if key in self.cache:
            return self.cache[key]
        out = []
        for p in self.tok.tokenize(word):
            if self.bert:
                initial, body = not p.startswith("##"), p[2:] if p.startswith("##") else p
            else:
                initial, body = p.startswith("▁"), p.lstrip("▁")
            if cap is None or len(body) <= cap:
                out.append(p)
                continue
            i = 0
            while i < len(body):
                for n in range(min(cap, len(body) - i), 0, -1):
                    cand = self._mark(body[i:i + n], initial, i == 0)
                    if cand in self.vocab:
                        out.append(cand)
                        i += n
                        break
                else:
                    if not self.bert and initial and i == 0 and "▁" in self.vocab:
                        out.append("▁")  # emit the bare word-start marker, retry the chunk unmarked
                        initial = False
                        continue
                    out.append(self.tok.unk_token)
                    i += 1
        self.cache[key] = out
        return out

    def words_to_ids(self, words, cap):
        """Returns (ids, index of the first piece of each word)."""
        ids, starts = [], []

            p = self.pieces(w, cap)
            if not p:
                continue
            starts.append(len(ids))
            ids.extend(self.tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(p))
        return ids, starts

    """Manual equivalent of train.encode() with a segmentation cap. Also returns token/word counts."""
    tok, feats, n_tok, n_word, n_unk = seg.tok, [], 0, 0, 0
    cls, sep = tok.cls_token_id, tok.sep_token_id

            else:

    rows = []
    for ck in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CKPT_DIR, "*_s*"))):
        tag = os.path.basename(ck)

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-25919/bundled-skills/2.1.293/4de0b1ad380c74374a7ad6743db019df/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
is system-agnostic - **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.

## How to use these values

Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
reference them by role throughout - so the light/dark values swap in one place,
and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:

```css
.viz-root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
  --text-secondary: #52514e;
  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
  /* ...only the roles this chart uses */
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
    --text-primary:   #ffffff;
    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
    --series-1:       #3987e5;
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
  --text-primary:   #ffffff;
  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
  --series-1:       #3987e5;
}
```

Declare the dark values under both scopes as above - the media query covers
the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
which must win both ways (the `:not(...)` guard lets a light stamp beat
OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).

## Categorical palette

Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
dark surface, not a separate palette:

| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
|------|-----|-------|------|
| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |

This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD Delta E 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
(OKLab ×100, >=8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision Delta E 19.6 light / 19.3
dark (>=15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors - with all 28 pairs in
play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule - so those
chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
in both modes** (worst pair CVD Delta E 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
light / 20.9 dark - clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
dark band (OKLCH L ~ 0.48-0.67, >= 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening -
the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex

  [PASS] Chroma floor           all 2 >= 0.1
  [PASS] CVD separation         worst adjacent #e0690a↔#2a78d6 ΔE 26.6 (protan) · tritan 31.4

"""Statistical analysis and figures. Reads results/model_outputs/*.json, results/language_features.csv
and results/intervention.csv; writes results/*.csv, results/stats.json, results/tables.md, figures/*.png.

The analysis follows planning.md: per model x task cell, languages are the unit of analysis.
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

from langs import FIGURES, RESULTS

RNG = np.random.default_rng(42)
B = 10_000
TASKS, MODELS = ["xnli", "ner", "sib"], ["mbert", "xlmr"]
TASK_NAME = {"xnli": "XNLI (accuracy)", "ner": "WikiANN NER (F1)", "sib": "SIB-200 (accuracy)"}
MODEL_NAME = {"mbert": "mBERT", "xlmr": "XLM-R"}
URIEL = ["dist_syntactic", "dist_phonological", "dist_inventory", "dist_genetic", "dist_geographic"]
PREDICTORS = {  # name -> columns
    "fertility": ["fert_ratio"], "syntactic": ["dist_syntactic"], "phonological": ["dist_phonological"],
    "inventory": ["dist_inventory"], "genetic": ["dist_genetic"], "geographic": ["dist_geographic"],
    "URIEL (all 5)": URIEL, "log pretrain size": ["log_size"], "non-Latin script": ["non_latin"],
}
# chart tokens (validated categorical slots 1-2; text and grid stay neutral)
C = {"mbert": "#2a78d6", "xlmr": "#eb6834", "ink": "#0b0b0b", "ink2": "#52514e", "grid": "#e4e3df", "surface": "#fcfcfb"}
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": C["surface"], "axes.facecolor": C["surface"], "savefig.facecolor": C["surface"],
                     "axes.edgecolor": C["grid"], "axes.labelcolor": C["ink2"], "xtick.color": C["ink2"],
                     "ytick.color": C["ink2"], "text.color": C["ink"], "axes.grid": True, "grid.color": C["grid"],
                     "grid.linewidth": 0.6, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "font.size": 9,
                     "axes.titlesize": 10, "axes.titleweight": "bold", "legend.frameon": False})


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- data
def load():
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RESULTS, "model_outputs", "*_s[0-9].json"))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        rows += [dict(task=d["task"], model=d["model"], seed=d["seed"], lang=l, score=s) for l, s in d["scores"].items()]
    raw = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    agg = raw.groupby(["task", "model", "lang"]).score.agg(score="mean", seed_sd="std", n_seeds="count").reset_index()
    en = agg[agg.lang == "en"].set_index(["task", "model"]).score
    agg["en_score"] = [en[(t, m)] for t, m in zip(agg.task, agg.model)]
    agg["drop"] = agg.en_score - agg.score
    agg["rel_drop"] = 100 * agg["drop"] / agg.en_score
    feats = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(RESULTS, "language_features.csv"))
    df = agg.merge(feats, on=["lang", "model"], validate="many_to_one")
    df["log_fert"] = np.log(df.fert_ratio)
    return raw, df


def cell(df, task, model, primary=True):
    d = df[(df.task == task) & (df.model == model) & (df.lang != "en")]
    return (d[d.unsegmented == 0] if primary else d).reset_index(drop=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statistics helpers
def r2(X, y, adjusted=False):
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(y)), X])
    res = y - X @ np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
    sst = ((y - y.mean()) ** 2).sum()
    if sst == 0:
        return np.nan
    v = 1 - (res ** 2).sum() / sst
    return 1 - (1 - v) * (len(y) - 1) / (len(y) - X.shape[1]) if adjusted else v


def boot(d, fn):
    """Percentile bootstrap over languages. fn(dataframe) -> scalar or vector."""
    n = len(d)
    out = np.array([fn(d.iloc[RNG.integers(0, n, n)]) for _ in range(B)], dtype=float)
    return np.nanpercentile(out, [2.5, 97.5], axis=0), out


def partial(d, target, controls, y="drop"):
    """Partial correlation of `target` with y given controls, with the OLS t-test p-value."""
    m = sm.OLS(d[y], sm.add_constant(d[[target] + controls])).fit()
    t = m.tvalues[target]
    return float(t / np.sqrt(t ** 2 + m.df_resid)), float(m.pvalues[target])


def fmt_ci(v, ci):
    return f"{v:.2f} [{ci[0]:.2f}, {ci[1]:.2f}]"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-cell analysis
def analyze_cell(d, fert="fert_ratio", y="drop"):
    yv, out = d[y].values, {"n": len(d)}
    out["drop_mean"], out["drop_sd"], out["drop_min"], out["drop_max"] = [float(f(yv)) for f in (np.mean, np.std, np.min, np.max)]
    preds = dict(PREDICTORS, fertility=[fert])
    # H1 / H2: variance explained by each predictor (set), with bootstrap CIs
    for name, cols in preds.items():
        adj = len(cols) > 1
        v = r2(d[cols].values, yv, adj)
        ci, _ = boot(d, lambda s, cols=cols, adj=adj: r2(s[cols].values, s[y].values, adj))
        out[f"r2|{name}"] = (float(v), ci.tolist())
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(d[fert], yv)
    rho, prho = stats.spearmanr(d[fert], yv)
    out.update(pearson_r=float(r), pearson_p=float(p), spearman=float(rho), spearman_p=float(prho))
    out["spearman_syntactic"] = float(stats.spearmanr(d.dist_syntactic, yv)[0])
    out["spearman_size"] = float(stats.spearmanr(d.log_size, yv)[0])
    for other in ("syntactic", "URIEL (all 5)", "log pretrain size"):
        cols, adj = preds[other], len(preds[other]) > 1
        ci, bs = boot(d, lambda s: r2(s[[fert]].values, s[y].values, adj) - r2(s[cols].values, s[y].values, adj))
        p_two = 2 * min((bs <= 0).mean(), (bs >= 0).mean())
        out[f"diff|{other}"] = (float(r2(d[[fert]].values, yv, adj) - r2(d[cols].values, yv, adj)), ci.tolist(), float(min(1, p_two)))
    # H4: does fertility survive controls?
    out["partial|size"] = partial(d, fert, ["log_size"], y)
    out["partial|size+syn"] = partial(d, fert, ["log_size", "dist_syntactic"], y)
    out["partial|size+syn+script"] = partial(d, fert, ["log_size", "dist_syntactic", "non_latin"], y)
    out["partial_syn|fert+size"] = partial(d, "dist_syntactic", [fert, "log_size"], y)
    out["partial_size|fert+syn"] = partial(d, "log_size", [fert, "dist_syntactic"], y)
    full = [fert, "log_size", "dist_syntactic"]
    out["r2_full"] = float(r2(d[full].values, yv))
    for c in full:
        out[f"unique|{c}"] = float(out["r2_full"] - r2(d[[x for x in full if x != c]].values, yv))
    z = d[[fert, "log_size"]].apply(lambda s: s - s.mean())
    z["inter"] = z[fert] * z.log_size
    m = sm.OLS(yv, sm.add_constant(z)).fit()
    out["interaction"] = (float(m.params["inter"]), float(m.pvalues["inter"]))
    out["corr_fert_size"] = float(stats.pearsonr(d[fert], d.log_size)[0])
    out["corr_fert_syn"] = float(stats.pearsonr(d[fert], d.dist_syntactic)[0])
    out["corr_fert_script"] = float(stats.pearsonr(d[fert], d.non_latin)[0])
    return out


def threshold(d, thr=2.5, fert="fert_ratio"):
    """H3: do languages above the fertility threshold fail catastrophically (>30)?"""
    hi, lo = d[d[fert] > thr], d[d[fert] <= thr]
    o = dict(n_above=len(hi), n_below=len(lo), above_langs=" ".join(hi.lang))
    for col, nm in (("drop", "abs"), ("rel_drop", "rel")):
        a, b = int((hi[col] > 30).sum()), int((lo[col] > 30).sum())
        o[f"above_{nm}>30"], o[f"below_{nm}>30"] = a, b
        o[f"fisher_p_{nm}"] = float(stats.fisher_exact([[a, len(hi) - a], [b, len(lo) - b]])[1]) if len(hi) else np.nan
    o["mean_drop_above"], o["mean_drop_below"] = float(hi["drop"].mean()) if len(hi) else np.nan, float(lo["drop"].mean())
    o["mean_rel_above"], o["mean_rel_below"] = float(hi.rel_drop.mean()) if len(hi) else np.nan, float(lo.rel_drop.mean())
    if len(hi) >= 2:  # nonlinearity: does a hinge at the threshold improve on a straight line?
        X = sm.add_constant(pd.DataFrame({"f": d[fert], "hinge": np.clip(d[fert] - thr, 0, None)}))
        m = sm.OLS(d["drop"], X).fit()
        o["hinge_coef"], o["hinge_p"] = float(m.params["hinge"]), float(m.pvalues["hinge"])
    return o


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- figures
def fig_scatter(df):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(13, 7.5))
    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS):
        for j, t in enumerate(TASKS):
            ax, d = axes[i, j], cell(df, t, m)
            ax.scatter(d.fert_ratio, d["drop"], s=26, color=C[m], edgecolor=C["surface"], linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
            b, a = np.polyfit(d.fert_ratio, d["drop"], 1)
            xs = np.array([d.fert_ratio.min(), d.fert_ratio.max()])
            ax.plot(xs, a + b * xs, color=C["ink2"], lw=1.5, zorder=2)
            ax.axvline(2.5, color=C["ink2"], lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=1)
            ax.axhline(30, color=C["ink2"], lw=1, ls=(0, (1, 3)), zorder=1)
            # direct labels only for the extremes
            lab = pd.concat([d.nlargest(4, "fert_ratio"), d.nlargest(3, "drop"), d.nsmallest(2, "drop")]).drop_duplicates("lang")
            for _, r in lab.iterrows():
                ax.annotate(r.lang, (r.fert_ratio, r["drop"]), xytext=(4, 3), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8, color=C["ink2"])
            ax.set_title(f"{MODEL_NAME[m]} · {TASK_NAME[t]}", loc="left")
            ax.text(0.03, 0.95, f"R² = {r2(d[['fert_ratio']].values, d['drop'].values):.2f}, n = {len(d)}",
                    transform=ax.transAxes, va="top", fontsize=9)
            ax.set_xlabel("Fertility ratio (subwords per word, relative to English)")
            ax.set_ylabel("Transfer drop vs. English (points)")
    fig.suptitle("Zero-shot transfer drop against tokenizer fertility. Dashed: the hypothesised 2.5x threshold; dotted: 30-point drop.",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.96))
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURES, "fig1_fertility_vs_drop.png"), dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_r2(stats_cells):
    names = ["fertility", "syntactic", "URIEL (all 5)", "log pretrain size", "non-Latin script"]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(13, 6), sharex=True)
    for i, m in enumerate(MODELS):
        for j, t in enumerate(TASKS):
            ax, s = axes[i, j], stats_cells[f"{t}|{m}"]
            v = np.array([s[f"r2|{n}"][0] for n in names])
            ci = np.array([s[f"r2|{n}"][1] for n in names])
            ypos = np.arange(len(names))[::-1]
            ax.barh(ypos, v, height=0.55, color=C[m], zorder=3)
            ax.hlines(ypos, ci[:, 0], ci[:, 1], color=C["ink"], lw=1.2, zorder=4)
            ax.axvspan(0.4, 0.6, color=C["grid"], alpha=0.6, zorder=0)
            ax.set_yticks(ypos, names if j == 0 else [""] * len(names))
            ax.set_xlim(-0.15, 1)
            ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
            ax.set_title(f"{MODEL_NAME[m]} · {TASK_NAME[t]} (n={s['n']})", loc="left")
            if i == 1:
                ax.set_xlabel("R² of transfer drop (adjusted R² for the 5-distance model)")
    fig.suptitle("Variance in transfer drop explained by each predictor alone. Lines: 95% bootstrap CI; grey band: hypothesised 40-60%.",
                 x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.95))
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURES, "fig2_r2_by_predictor.png"), dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_contrast(con):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4))
    for ax, t in zip(axes, TASKS):
        d = con[con.task == t]
        ax.scatter(d.d_fert, d.d_drop, s=26, color=C["ink2"], edgecolor=C["surface"], linewidth=0.8, zorder=3)
        ax.axhline(0, color=C["ink2"], lw=0.8)
        for _, r in pd.concat([d.nlargest(4, "d_fert"), d.nlargest(2, "d_drop"), d.nsmallest(2, "d_drop")]).drop_duplicates("lang").iterrows():
            ax.annotate(r.lang, (r.d_fert, r.d_drop), xytext=(4, 3), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8, color=C["ink2"])
        r, _ = stats.pearsonr(d.d_fert, d.d_drop)
        ax.set_title(f"{TASK_NAME[t]}", loc="left")
        ax.text(0.03, 0.95, f"r = {r:.2f}, n = {len(d)}", transform=ax.transAxes, va="top")
        ax.set_xlabel("Fertility ratio: mBERT minus XLM-R")
        ax.set_ylabel("Transfer drop: mBERT minus XLM-R (points)")
    fig.suptitle("Same language, two tokenizers: does the model that fragments a language more also lose more on it?", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.94))
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURES, "fig3_within_language_contrast.png"), dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


def fig_intervention(df, iv):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4.2))
    for ax, t in zip(axes, TASKS):
        for m in MODELS:
            d = cell(df, t, m)
            ax.scatter(d.fert_ratio, d["drop"], s=16, facecolor="none", edgecolor=C[m], linewidth=0.9, alpha=0.7, zorder=2,
                       label=f"{MODEL_NAME[m]}: other languages (observed)")
            g = iv[(iv.task == t) & (iv.model == m)]
            ax.errorbar(g.fert_ratio, g["drop"], yerr=g.drop_sd, color=C[m], lw=2, marker="o", ms=5, zorder=3,
                        label=f"{MODEL_NAME[m]}: English, over-segmented (intervention)")
            last = g.iloc[-1]
            ax.annotate(MODEL_NAME[m], (last.fert_ratio, last["drop"]), xytext=(5, 0), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8, color=C["ink2"])
        ax.set_title(TASK_NAME[t], loc="left")
        ax.set_xlabel("Fertility ratio relative to standard English tokenization")
        ax.set_ylabel("Drop vs. standard English score (points)")
        ax.set_xlim(0.8, 4.2)
    axes[0].legend(fontsize=7.5, loc="upper left")
    fig.suptitle("Forcing finer segmentation of English at test time (lines) vs. the cross-lingual pattern (hollow points)", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.94))
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURES, "fig4_intervention.png"), dpi=160)
    plt.close(fig)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
def main():
    os.makedirs(FIGURES, exist_ok=True)
    raw, df = load()
    df.to_csv(os.path.join(RESULTS, "transfer_results.csv"), index=False)
    S, md = {"cells": {}, "threshold": {}, "robust": {}}, []
    cells = [(t, m) for t in TASKS for m in MODELS if len(cell(df, t, m))]

    # --- descriptive
    desc = []
    for t, m in cells:
        d, a = cell(df, t, m), cell(df, t, m, primary=False)
        desc.append(dict(task=t, model=m, seeds=int(a.n_seeds.max()), en_score=a.en_score.iloc[0], n_targets=len(a),
                         mean_target=a.score.mean(), mean_drop=a["drop"].mean(), sd_drop=a["drop"].std(), min_drop=a["drop"].min(),
                         max_drop=a["drop"].max(), worst=a.loc[a["drop"].idxmax(), "lang"], mean_seed_sd=a.seed_sd.mean(),
                         fert_min=d.fert_ratio.min(), fert_median=d.fert_ratio.median(), fert_max=d.fert_ratio.max()))
    desc = pd.DataFrame(desc)
    md += ["## Descriptive (all targets; fertility columns on whitespace-segmented targets)", desc.round(2).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- primary per-cell analysis
    for t, m in cells:
        d = cell(df, t, m)
        S["cells"][f"{t}|{m}"] = analyze_cell(d)
        S["threshold"][f"{t}|{m}"] = threshold(d)
        print("analyzed", t, m, flush=True)
    keys = list(S["cells"])
    for fam in ("pearson_p", "spearman_p"):
        adj = multipletests([S["cells"][k][fam] for k in keys], method="holm")[1]
        for k, a in zip(keys, adj):
            S["cells"][k][fam + "_holm"] = float(a)
    for fam in ("partial|size", "partial|size+syn", "partial|size+syn+script"):
        adj = multipletests([S["cells"][k][fam][1] for k in keys], method="holm")[1]
        for k, a in zip(keys, adj):
            S["cells"][k][fam + "|holm"] = float(a)
    adj = multipletests([S["cells"][k]["diff|syntactic"][2] for k in keys], method="holm")[1]
    for k, a in zip(keys, adj):
        S["cells"][k]["diff|syntactic|holm"] = float(a)

    rows = []
    for k in keys:
        s = S["cells"][k]
        rows.append({"cell": k, "n": s["n"], **{n: fmt_ci(*s[f"r2|{n}"]) for n in PREDICTORS}})
    md += ["## H1/H2: R² of drop by single predictor (95% bootstrap CI); 'URIEL (all 5)' is adjusted R²", pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False)]
    rows = []
    for k in keys:
        s = S["cells"][k]
        rows.append({"cell": k, "pearson r": round(s["pearson_r"], 2), "p (Holm)": f"{s['pearson_p_holm']:.3g}",
                     "spearman fert": round(s["spearman"], 2), "p (Holm) ": f"{s['spearman_p_holm']:.3g}",
                     "spearman syntactic": round(s["spearman_syntactic"], 2), "spearman log size": round(s["spearman_size"], 2),
                     "R²(fert)-R²(syn)": fmt_ci(*s["diff|syntactic"][:2]), "p boot (Holm)": f"{s['diff|syntactic|holm']:.3g}",
                     "adjR²(fert)-adjR²(URIEL5)": fmt_ci(*s["diff|URIEL (all 5)"][:2]),
                     "R²(fert)-R²(size)": fmt_ci(*s["diff|log pretrain size"][:2])})
    md += ["## H1/H2: correlations and R² differences", pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False)]
    rows = []
    for k in keys:
        s = S["cells"][k]
        rows.append({"cell": k, "r(fert,size)": round(s["corr_fert_size"], 2), "r(fert,syn)": round(s["corr_fert_syn"], 2),
                     "r(fert,non-Latin)": round(s["corr_fert_script"], 2),
                     "partial r fert|size": f"{s['partial|size'][0]:.2f} (p_holm={s['partial|size|holm']:.3g})",
                     "fert|size+syn": f"{s['partial|size+syn'][0]:.2f} (p_holm={s['partial|size+syn|holm']:.3g})",
                     "fert|size+syn+script": f"{s['partial|size+syn+script'][0]:.2f} (p_holm={s['partial|size+syn+script|holm']:.3g})",
                     "syn|fert+size": f"{s['partial_syn|fert+size'][0]:.2f} (p={s['partial_syn|fert+size'][1]:.3g})",
                     "size|fert+syn": f"{s['partial_size|fert+syn'][0]:.2f} (p={s['partial_size|fert+syn'][1]:.3g})",
                     "R² full": round(s["r2_full"], 2), "unique fert": round(s["unique|fert_ratio"], 3),
                     "unique size": round(s["unique|log_size"], 3), "unique syn": round(s["unique|dist_syntactic"], 3),
                     "fert x size (p)": f"{s['interaction'][0]:.2f} ({s['interaction'][1]:.3g})"})
    md += ["## H4: fertility vs. pretraining size and syntactic distance (full model = fert + log size + syntactic)", pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False)]
    md += ["## H3: 2.5x threshold (primary fertility, whitespace-segmented targets)",
           pd.DataFrame([{"cell": k, **v} for k, v in S["threshold"].items()]).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)]
    # the same threshold on the parallel token ratio over all targets
    md += ["## H3 on the parallel token ratio (all targets, incl. zh/ja/th/my)",
           pd.DataFrame([{"cell": f"{t}|{m}", **threshold(cell(df, t, m, primary=False), fert="par_ratio")} for t, m in cells]).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- pooled across cells, cluster bootstrap by language
    pool = pd.concat([cell(df, t, m).assign(cellid=f"{t}|{m}") for t, m in cells])
    zc = ["drop", "fert_ratio", "log_size", "dist_syntactic"]
    pool[[c + "_z" for c in zc]] = pool.groupby("cellid")[zc].transform(lambda s: (s - s.mean()) / s.std())
    langs = pool.lang.unique()
    by_lang = {l: g for l, g in pool.groupby("lang")}

    def pooled_fit(p):
        o = [r2(p[["fert_ratio_z"]].values, p.drop_z.values), r2(p[["dist_syntactic_z"]].values, p.drop_z.values),
             r2(p[["log_size_z"]].values, p.drop_z.values)]
        X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(p)), p[["fert_ratio_z", "log_size_z", "dist_syntactic_z"]].values])
        return o + list(np.linalg.lstsq(X, p.drop_z.values, rcond=None)[0][1:])
    est = pooled_fit(pool)
    bs = np.array([pooled_fit(pd.concat([by_lang[l] for l in RNG.choice(langs, len(langs))])) for _ in range(2000)])
    ci = np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5], axis=0).T
    names = ["R² fertility", "R² syntactic", "R² log size", "beta fertility (joint)", "beta log size (joint)", "beta syntactic (joint)"]
    S["pooled"] = {n: (float(e), c.tolist()) for n, e, c in zip(names, est, ci)}
    d_fs = bs[:, 0] - bs[:, 1]
    S["pooled"]["R² fert - R² syn"] = (float(est[0] - est[1]), np.percentile(d_fs, [2.5, 97.5]).tolist())
    d_fz = bs[:, 0] - bs[:, 2]
    S["pooled"]["R² fert - R² size"] = (float(est[0] - est[2]), np.percentile(d_fz, [2.5, 97.5]).tolist())
    md += [f"## Pooled over all cells (z-scored within cell, n={len(pool)} rows, {len(langs)} languages, cluster bootstrap by language)",
           pd.DataFrame([{"quantity": k, "estimate [95% CI]": fmt_ci(*v)} for k, v in S["pooled"].items()]).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- within-language tokenizer contrast
    feats_z = df.copy()
    feats_z["size_z"] = feats_z.groupby(["task", "model"]).log_size.transform(lambda s: (s - s.mean()) / s.std())
    con_rows, con_all = [], []
    for t in TASKS:
        a, b = [feats_z[(feats_z.task == t) & (feats_z.model == m) & (feats_z.lang != "en") & (feats_z.unsegmented == 0)].set_index("lang") for m in MODELS]
        if not len(a) or not len(b):
            continue
        c = pd.DataFrame({"task": t, "d_fert": a.fert_ratio - b.fert_ratio, "d_drop": a["drop"] - b["drop"], "d_size": a.size_z - b.size_z}).reset_index()
        con_all.append(c)
        r, p = stats.pearsonr(c.d_fert, c.d_drop)
        rho, prho = stats.spearmanr(c.d_fert, c.d_drop)
        ci, _ = boot(c, lambda s: stats.pearsonr(s.d_fert, s.d_drop)[0])
        pr, pp = partial(c, "d_fert", ["d_size"], y="d_drop")
        con_rows.append({"task": t, "n": len(c), "mean d_fert": c.d_fert.mean(), "mean d_drop": c.d_drop.mean(), "pearson r [CI]": fmt_ci(r, ci),
                         "p": p, "spearman": rho, "spearman p": prho, "partial r | d_size": pr, "partial p": pp})
    con = pd.concat(con_all)
    con.to_csv(os.path.join(RESULTS, "within_language_contrast.csv"), index=False)
    S["contrast"] = con_rows
    md += ["## Within-language contrast (mBERT minus XLM-R, same language and test set)", pd.DataFrame(con_rows).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- robustness of H1 to analysis choices
    variants = {
        "primary (fert_ratio, abs drop)": dict(),
        "relative drop (%)": dict(y="rel_drop"),
        "log fertility": dict(fert="log_fert"),
        "parallel token ratio, all targets": dict(fert="par_ratio", primary=False),
        "NER: fertility on WikiANN words": dict(fert="ner_fert_ratio", only="ner"),
        "NER: test sets >= 1000 sentences": dict(only="ner", min_n=1000),
        "Latin-script targets only": dict(script=0),
        "non-Latin targets only": dict(script=1),
    }
    rows = []
    for name, v in variants.items():
        row = {"variant": name}
        for t, m in cells:
            if v.get("only") and t != v["only"]:
                row[f"{t}|{m}"] = ""
                continue
            d = cell(df, t, m, v.get("primary", True))
            if "min_n" in v:
                d = d[d.ner_test_n >= v["min_n"]]
            if "script" in v:
                d = d[d.non_latin == v["script"]]
            if len(d) < 6:
                row[f"{t}|{m}"] = f"n={len(d)}"
                continue
            f, y = v.get("fert", "fert_ratio"), v.get("y", "drop")
            val = r2(d[[f]].values, d[y].values)
            ci, _ = boot(d, lambda s: r2(s[[f]].values, s[y].values))
            syn = r2(d[["dist_syntactic"]].values, d[y].values)
            row[f"{t}|{m}"] = f"{fmt_ci(val, ci)}; syn {syn:.2f}; n={len(d)}"
            S["robust"][f"{name}|{t}|{m}"] = (float(val), ci.tolist(), float(syn), len(d))
        rows.append(row)
    md += ["## Robustness: R²(fertility) [CI]; R²(syntactic); n", pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- measurement noise in the drops (binomial sampling of the test set, accuracy tasks)
    rows = []
    for t, m in cells:
        d = cell(df, t, m)
        if t == "ner":
            continue
        n_test = 5010 if t == "xnli" else 204
        p_t, p_e = d.score / 100, d.en_score / 100
        noise = (1e4 * (p_t * (1 - p_t) + p_e * (1 - p_e)) / n_test).mean()
        rows.append({"cell": f"{t}|{m}", "n_test": n_test, "var(drop)": d["drop"].var(), "sampling var": noise,
                     "reliability": 1 - noise / d["drop"].var(), "mean seed SD": d.seed_sd.mean()})
    md += ["## Noise ceiling: share of between-language drop variance not due to test-set sampling", pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- error analysis: where does the fertility model miss?
    rows = []
    for t, m in cells:
        d = cell(df, t, m).copy()
        b, a = np.polyfit(d.fert_ratio, d["drop"], 1)
        d["resid"] = d["drop"] - (a + b * d.fert_ratio)
        rows.append({"cell": f"{t}|{m}", "slope (pts per 1.0 fertility)": round(b, 1),
                     "worse than fertility predicts": ", ".join(f"{r.lang} (+{r.resid:.0f})" for r in d.nlargest(5, "resid").itertuples()),
                     "better than fertility predicts": ", ".join(f"{r.lang} ({r.resid:.0f})" for r in d.nsmallest(5, "resid").itertuples()),
                     "mean resid Latin": round(d[d.non_latin == 0].resid.mean(), 1), "mean resid non-Latin": round(d[d.non_latin == 1].resid.mean(), 1)})
    md += ["## Error analysis: residuals of drop ~ fertility", pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False)]

    # --- intervention
    ipath = os.path.join(RESULTS, "intervention.csv")
    if os.path.exists(ipath):
        iv = pd.read_csv(ipath).groupby(["task", "model", "cap"]).agg(fert_ratio=("fert_ratio", "mean"), drop=("drop", "mean"),
                                                                      drop_sd=("drop", "std"), score=("score", "mean"),
                                                                      unk_rate=("unk_rate", "mean"), seeds=("seed", "count")).reset_index()
        iv = iv.sort_values(["task", "model", "fert_ratio"]).fillna({"drop_sd": 0})
        # cross-lingual drop predicted at the same fertility by the cell's regression line
        pred = []
        for r in iv.itertuples():
            d = cell(df, r.task, r.model)
            b, a = np.polyfit(d.fert_ratio, d["drop"], 1)
            pred.append(a + b * r.fert_ratio)
        iv["crosslingual_fit_at_same_fertility"] = pred
        iv.to_csv(os.path.join(RESULTS, "intervention_summary.csv"), index=False)
        md += ["## Intervention: over-segmenting English at test time (cap = max characters per subword, 0 = standard)", iv.round(2).to_markdown(index=False)]
        fig_intervention(df, iv)

    fig_scatter(df)
    fig_r2(S["cells"])
    fig_contrast(con)
    json.dump(S, open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "stats.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    open(os.path.join(RESULTS, "tables.md"), "w").write("\n\n".join(md) + "\n")
    print("\n\n".join(md))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
